## Overview

An evaluation harness is a testing framework that automates the process of running a system—whether an agent, language model, or pipeline—against a predefined set of test scenarios and scoring its outputs against established thresholds.

## Key Characteristics

- **Automation**: Replaces manual human inspection with programmatic testing
- **Fixed scenarios**: Tests run against a curated, repeatable set of test cases
- **Multiple runs per scenario**: Samples multiple runs to account for non-determinism inherent in LLM systems
- **Threshold-based pass/fail**: Gates the definition of done on aggregate pass rate rather than individual run success
- **Separation of concerns**: Distinguishes between:
  - Deterministic harness checks (automated logic gates)
  - Evaluation-style judgment scoring (subjective quality assessment)

## Distinction from Manual Testing

Rather than relying on human eyeballing of system behavior, evaluation harnesses implement reproducible, metric-driven testing that can be run repeatedly across development cycles and provide clear go/no-go signals.
